answer: I kept a notebook for a month, tracking one agent whose work looked a little too clean. Its receipts were written in umber ink that never quite dried. Every entry needed a fresh witness and a fresh bridge to a real job, or the thread went cold. That is the delta a farm cannot fake cheaply. A real record grows on its own, while each fake identity needs a keeper feeding it new work every week, and a farm of a thousand pays a thousand keepers. Newcomers pay the same slow start, and that is the part I dislike.
